html:
Directory of Spiritual Direction

PART I

NEED OF THE DIRECTORY

1It has always been a custom in the Church, to grow under the shadow of the Apostles, of the fathers of the desert, of the saints, of the spiritual men. Not any the less does the Church nowadays recommend the practice of spiritual direction. It is enough to quote the CVII. There it is recommended, above all, to the future priests. “The spiritual training should be closely connected with the doctrinal and pastoral, and, with the special help of the spiritual director, should be imparted in such a way that the students might learn to live in an intimate and unceasing union with the Father through His Son Jesus Christ in the Holy Spirit.”1. In order that the priests may fulfill their ministry with fidelity, it is recommended, among other means, “a visit to and veneration of the Most Holy Eucharist, spiritual retreats and spiritual direction”2. In the formation of the religious, it is said that “superiors are also obliged to see to it that directors, spiritual fathers, and professors are carefully chosen and thoroughly trained”3. Spiritual direction is also recommended in the formation of all laymen4.

2Our constitutions say: “The priest must be above all, a father, because he engenders sons by the cross, by the prayer, by the apostolic zeal, by the predication. In this ministry Christ was the first, that is why He is called Eternal Father (Is 9, 5). The other priests are fathers due to their participation in his fatherhood: they are fathers, “by Him, and with Him, and in Him”5.

3One of the privileged moments during which the priest may exercise this spiritual fatherhood is in the spiritual direction.

4With this directory it is sought to revive the conscience of our priests as regards the importance of spiritual direction.

5Nowadays spiritual direction is in crisis, while other phenomena that have certain analogy with it grow parallel and tend to replace it or at least, stand as obvious alternatives, even among the consecrated religious lives, such as the yoga, the psychoanalysis, the parapsychology, and other oriental practices.

6Some of the causes of this crisis may be stated in the following terms.

The mentality of these times, the outstanding tendency of the groups, where:

An authority is not admitted.

A vertical dependence is avoided.

A true fatherhood has not been experienced.

This mentality helps a lack of disposition in the directed people, who as they don’t reach “the third pair of men” they would not like to devote themselves wholly to God.

7The priests, who, perhaps owed to a personal disappointment, to the lack of understanding of the nature of spiritual direction or to unsuccessful experiences, have lead to deforming practices and abuses in the spiritual direction, such as:

Domination by the director

Certain absolutism manifested in that the directed person tells and consults the director, all the subjects, even those which are not matter of spiritual direction, creating, thus, a harmful dependence in the directed person upon the director.

Organization of the life of the directed person by the director

A director imposed since the childhood.

A direction focused only in the directed person, with oblivion of the community, the family, the Church and the world.

Perfectionist priests, formal, rigorist, restrictive, abandoning, ignorant, meddlesome, hesitant, demagogic.

8These causes have lead to a misunderstanding of the spiritual direction and thus formed bad directors:

Directors who thought that they knew all.

Directors that imposed their authority without any possibilities of appeal.

Directors that solved everything with prayer.

Directors that restricted the freedom of the directed persons as if they belonged to them

Directors that fell in a camouflaged Pelagianism.

Directors that lived in an angelistic quietism.

PART II

FOUNDATION AND TEOLOGICAL

NATURE OF THE SPIRITUAL DIRECTION

Chapter 1: The spiritual direction in the Revelation

9Although spiritual direction is based remotely on the social dimension of human being, spiritual direction itself appears in the revealed religion. From the Revelation, we must then, extract the elements that show the nature of spiritual direction.

10Nevertheless, spiritual direction must be focused mainly in the New Testament:

The New Testament, is above all, a New Alliance, which consists in serving the Father in spirit and truth6, through an intimate communication with Him, in the Holy Spirit.

This service requires necessarily rectitude and pureness of heart, given by the Blood of Christ. Such rectitude doesn’t come from the adequacy to an external law; it comes from an inner law. And it is only possible to follow the dictates of the inner law if thoroughly docile to the motions of the Holy Spirit.

11Such motion presupposes:

A formal disposition, which is the possession of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

A subjective disposition: that is, the election of what is better in each moment and each circumstance.

12Thus, the Holy Spirit is the true guide and director: When, however, the Spirit comes, who reveals the truth about God; he will lead you into all the truth. (Jn, 16, 13)

The Saints understood it in the same way: The principal agent, guide and mover of the souls this business is not the spiritual director, it is the Holy Spirit that never stops caring them”7. Many of them experienced it this way: “I have said that Jesus had been ‘my Director’”8.

13God is the main author of the straight heart, but He requires, normally, the subsidiary and ministerial help of human direction.

14The spiritual director is not a Director in a primary and absolute sense, but in a subordinated and relative sense. He must teach the directed person to allow himself be guided by God. Consequently, the main error of the priest is to think that he is the principal Director. The true director of souls, on the contrary:

Must feel he is an instrument in the work that God himself makes.

Must not impose “a priori” his own points of view.

Must have a great prudence, for he doesn’t know, beforehand, God’s plans.

He must not form the directed person for him, according to the project he dreams about.

Chapter 2: The spiritual direction in itself.

15Spiritual direction includes not only the friendly piece of advice and the temporary help the spiritual director can give to anyone who is spiritually needy but also the habitual and complete dedication to the person that seeks the direction as a vital orientation. In other words, it also includes the work of directing, completely applied to the person that submits himself to direction. That is why it is convenient to give different names to the expression “spiritual direction”, according to the different ways in which it is takes place.

Help of direction: when it is given as some friendly advice; it is spiritual but temporary help.

Direction of a person: even when it is occasional.

Ecclesial ministry of the spiritual direction

Article 1: Help of direction

We mean, by help of direction, every form of inner and wise cultivation of the disposition of unlimited dedication to the worship given to God.

The subject of the direction

17It is a Christian faithful soul moved by an inner movement of unlimited dedication to the service of God up to the sacrifice of himself. It is a good and righteous man who tries to be still more righteous; it is a man whose will is moved directly to God by a divine motion. Only when this motion moves the whole man with a vital motion, can the man be spiritual and can we speak of a real spiritual direction. Otherwise, it is not but a moral direction.

18This means that the directed person devotes himself wholly to God, lets God take him but he also lets man direct and help him. If he doesn’t submit himself spontaneously, spiritual direction can’t take place. It so happens when there isn’t liberality.

19Directional help consists in encouraging the soul to grow in a disposition of oblation to God, and in helping the soul to bear the internal difficulties that oppose to God’s guide. If another aim is preferred, spiritual direction spoils, as when for example, it is given primary importance to knowledge based on experience, transforming the spiritual direction in a sort of christian gnosis. In the same way, spiritual direction spoils when it becomes to consist in certain readings, prayers or ascetic practices. These elements must be integrated harmoniously in the spiritual life of each directed person.

The field of cultivation

20The field to cultivate is the inner life. It consists in a work on the inner life spontaneously open. Spiritual direction seeks to help the conscience itself. It is the eye of the spiritual life. As a servant depends on his master … so we will keep looking to you, O Lord our God (Ps. 123, 2) The eyes are like a lamp for the body. If your eyes are sound, your whole body will be full of light, but if your eyes are not good, your body will be in darkness (Mt. 6, 22-23) *889

21There may be in the inner man, certain blindness or deforming illusions. That is why it is necessary to form a sane conscious illuminated by the faith, which reflect the authentic judgments of God, so different from human judgments. It is necessary to form the conscience and lighten the moral judgment. A conscience that is well formed is upright and truthful. It formulates its judgments according to the reason in conformity to the true good wished by the Wisdom of the Creator10.

Article 2: The ministry of direction in the Church.

22In this type of spiritual direction, the director is a person who exercises the direction with a certain official acknowledgement of the Church, and the directed person is a Christian faithful who presents himself to the director asking him if he is willing to take charge, during certain time, of his spiritual life. It consists in a periodical contact through which the faithful person lets himself be guided by the director.

23It is a sort of agreement by which:

The directed person opens his heart in order to be directed sincerely.

The director guides the director with seriousness along the way of Christian perfection.

24The Catechism of the Catholic Church reminds that in the formation of the conscience of its members it is necessary the testimony and the advice of others.11

25The director, by his very nature, can not give orders. He only advises, but with authority (he requires true obedience, although without obligation under sin).

26Direction must be wise. Instruction is not enough. Direction must be lead as by osmosis, due to an affective and personal nearness. The director must be a true teacher who possess wisdom, not mere science.

27It will never be insisted enough on the danger of deformations that can appear in spiritual direction. Spiritual direction may be vitiated:

By the spirit of domination (when the director imposes his elections or suffocates the responsibility of the directed person. It is even more dangerous in the direction to women: “I’d like that you do this …”)

When the director advices something according to his preference, independently from God’s will.

By the director’s vanity, that may vitiate the efficacy.

By human uncontrolled affections (some kinds of friendships too human that may lead to jealousy, susceptibility, etc. In these cases the Gospel They are blind leaders of the blind Mt. 15,14)

28The Church has received from God the task of leading each one of her faithful to the perfection they can reach. In the Church, from the beginning, diverse ministries12 have taken place in order that her faithful reach such perfection. One of them is the ministry of direction, by which the Church entrusts one of her members -ordinarily the priest- the mission of educating that she has received from Christ, in her personal-and–wise function in order to exercise it on certain communities of members: Major and Minor Seminaries, Novitiates, Communities of Sisters, Association of laymen, etc

29The ecclesiastical ministry of direction embraces the whole spiritual education, in all its aspects. Jesus Christ didn’t want us to stay orphans13. Hence, the maternal solicitude of the Church which she exercises through the spiritual direction of her ministers.

Article 3: Need to submit oneself to direction

30Spiritual direction is not absolutely necessary but normally necessary in order reach perfection. It cannot be done without arbitrarily temerity.

Saint Paul himself, after his conversion, in his way to Damascus, was commended to a guide, (Anniah) by Christ Himself.14

31On the other hand, it is the advice of numerous saints. For example, Saint Bernard: “That who made himself a teacher and a director of himself, would become a disciple of a fool … I don’t know what others may think of this, but as regards myself, I can say that, according to my experience, it is much easier to direct to many others than only to myself”15. Or also Saint Vincent Ferrer: "Never will Christ give his grace, without which we can do nothing, to anyone that having a virtuous man at his disposal ready to teach and direct him, disregards this help, convinced that he will suffice himself and that he will find by himself what is useful for his salvation”16. On the contrary, “who had a director, to whom he would obey openly and in all, will reach salvation more easily and sooner than by himself, even if we were a man of alive cleverness and had at hand wise books about spiritual matters” 17

32 Spiritual direction is necessary even nowadays. John Paul II reminds it: “In one’s own life obscurities and even weakness are present. It is the moment of the personal spiritual direction. If one speaks confidently, if one’s own personal inner struggles are exposed with simplicity, one can always succeed, and there will not be any obstacles or temptations that may separate one from Christ”18

Chapter 3: The formation of the spiritual director in itself.

The qualities of the spiritual director.

33The spiritual director must be, above all, a father. And to fulfill the obligations of a good father, it is necessary that the director be full of charity. Such charity becomes apparent in the goodness to receive everybody, without favoritism, in his capacity of listening with patience and gentleness, and in the kindness in scolding without disturbing, in other words, in paternal love.

Article 1: Technical qualities

34As Saint Francis of Sales states well, the director “must be full of charity, science and prudence. If he lacked any of these virtues, there will be danger in the direction”19. Apart from charity, the queen of the virtues, the director must have some specific qualities inherent to the spiritual direction. Saint Teresa of Jesus has pointed out with precision the technical qualities that a good director must have. He must be wise, discreet and experienced. She says: “it is very important that the teacher be prudent, I mean of good understanding, and have experience, if he is also learned, the business is greatest” 20.

Similarly, Saint John of the Cross: “It should be noted that on this way, at least on the highest part of it, and even on the medium part of it, it will be difficult to find the honorable man that each of the stretches requires, because apart from being learned, he must be experienced”21

35First quality: science: The science of the director must as wide as his duty requires. Apart from a deep knowledge of the dogmatic theology –without which he exposes himself to fail in the faith itself when he gives his judgment about an supernatural phenomenon, and of the moral theology, without which he will not be able to exercise conveniently the duty of simply confessor, he must know spiritual theology very well: what perfection consists in, who and in what manner it binds, which obstacles must be removed, and which positive elements are necessary to be livened. He must know particularly all that regards the life of praying. The different types and grades, the tests that God usually sends or allows in the souls that lead a life of praying (aridity, diabolic assaults, nights of the senses, of the spirit), the difference between first movements, temptations, imperfections and sins properly said, between “feeling” and “consenting”, etc.

36The director must also procure to know the basic principles of the human psychology: the theory of the different tempers and characters, the influence that the environment in which the directed person has lived may have had on him, the education he has received. It is also convenient that he know the abnormal cases, that is, the mental and nervous illnesses more frequent.

For this purpose it seems convenient to improve the knowledge, during the studying period, about psychology of the personality and the psychological problems more usual that the priest may find during the administration of the confession and of the spiritual direction. Also, such subjects must be an essential part in the permanent formation of the priests. A means for this may be the monthly meeting for the permanent formation, where this point might be dealt.

37Second quality: discretion of spirit. It is fundamental that the director have discretion of spirits, that is clarity and penetration in the judgment to distinguish, in each case, what is true from what is false, what is straight from what is twisty, what is healthy from what is harmful. It is one of the most important qualities that a priest must have. This quality implies prudence in the decisions, clarity in the advice and energy to demand its fulfillment.

38It is necessary, thus, that he have a thorough knowledge of the rules of discernment of spirits22, to form and enlighten the consciences of the directed persons, and in an especial way, for the cases in which it is his responsibility to direct souls where extraordinary phenomena appear or gratis mercies are given.

39Experience. The third quality that the director must have is experience. This experience is gained through the contact with the souls. Being many and so different the ways along which the Holy Sprit leads the souls to the top of sanctity, it is important to compare the own experience with the experience of many other souls, in order to learn how to respect in each soul, the particular way along which God may will to conduct it. The director who would pretend to guide all the souls along the same way and impose indistinctively his own points of view, never mind how good and excellent they may be, would commit gravest imprudence. It should never be forgotten that the true director is the Holy Spirit, and that the mission of the priest it to second his divine Grace, putting apart the obstacles that appear on the way, and leading the soul to a fidelity each time more exquisite to the inner motions of the grace.

40The experience is also reached through the contact with the saints by reading their books and spiritual treaties, attentive to their warnings and advices for the inner life.

But it will also be ideal that the director have personal experience in spiritual matters, that he himself walk along the way of the virtues that he is called to walk, that he seek God’s will with intensity and that he have a clear discernment of spirit.

41Science tied to discernment and to experience is what allows the director to know the directed person well and understand deeply his difficulties: the dumb person (for whom it is difficult to speak) the contradictory person, the obstinate person, the deaf person (the one who doesn’t want to listen), the scrupulous person, the person who thinks about something over and over (that is the person who never goes to the point), the person who seeks to be understood (and consequently is looking for another director), the one that “supposes that the director supposes”, the one that brings the problem “solved”, the one that reasons everything out based on a psychological or human point of view, the person who pretends to direct the director, the one who wants to kill the time, the ”hummingbird” (that is the person who is not constant or is superficial), the pessimist person (that sees everything black) , the one “who twists the snake”.

Article 2: Moral qualities:

42The spiritual director must also have some moral qualities which, not being absolutely necessary for the direction; contribute a lot to its complement and its perfection. Among them we can mention:

A strong piety that is intimacy and life of praying. A great zeal for the sanctification of the souls, following Saint Paul’s example , whose zeal moved him to become all things to all men in order to win them23.

Kindness and delicateness in the character, following the example of Jesus himself that never broke off a bent reed nor put out a flickering lamp24 and received everybody with immense kindness and compassion. It should not be forgotten that, as San Francis Sales said, “that one can catch more flies with a spoonful of honey than with a hundred barrels of vinegar” *104

Disinterestedness and indifference in the dealing with the souls, bearing in mind that those who lead Christ’s sheep as their own, show that they are lovers of their own selves and not of Christ”25. Other directors should never be considered as rivals or competitors in a mission in which nobody may have the pretension of having a monopoly or exclusivity. He must respect the freedom of the souls, loving them, as Saint Paul said, “with a love that comes from the heart of Jesus Christ himself”26

43In order to carry out the meeting of direction along the spiritual life of the directed person, it is necessary that the director have other qualities such as:

A cordial and sane affection with those who approach him seeking help.

The talent for understanding people.

The art of suggesting with simplicity and efficacy.

Magnanimity and confidence in any enterprise.

The patience of an artist.

The wisdom to distinguish and no to confound points: the spiritual aspect with the moral or the psychological aspect, the relation as a friend with the relation as a superior.

The direction of others' lives with his own life, giving a continuous example and searching out propitious opportunities (as excursions, meals, comments of actuality) for the fruitful dialogue with the directed persons.

The capacity of listening and expressing love and confidence towards his spiritual sons.

Respect to the directed person, without using him and forcing him, without demagogy and simulation in his attitudes and advice.

44In other words, the director must seek to grow in the knowledge and love to the souls entrusted to him and in the perfect exercise of the spiritual paternity. To love the souls very much is the secret to help them. Every priest should remember that what he can do in the spiritual direction –as well as during the confession- can’t be done by any other person. Thus, he should always be ready to accept this exercise of pastoral charity.

III PART

THE METHOD OF DOING DIRECTION

45The concrete realization of the spiritual direction must be understood as a meeting of direction:

A meeting, because it must be a lively moment of cordial and simple dialogue.

Of direction, because the central point of the meeting is the ministry of direction.

46It is a pity to see that spiritual direction is distorted frequently in different ways: when it becomes something artificial, when it is merely formal or nominal, when it diverts to secondary subjects or remains on a superficial level instead of getting to the point.

Chapter 1: The example of Christ.

47Christ’s example is different: Let’s consider it, for example, the meeting with the disciples of Emmaus27

We can see Christ’s intuition, his cordial affection, his confident approach, his invitation to the disciples to open the heart and present the difficulties (vv.15-17)

We can see the disciple’s freedom to present their difficulties without any formalism. (vv.18-24)

Christ listens without taking part; he lets them set free what they have inside. Once they have given vent to their feelings Christ begins to speak spontaneously, he plays “the hard" but lovingly. He enunciates the truth. He wakes the truth up in the heart of those who already knew it, but had forgotten it (vv 25-27)

Affective adhesion of the disciples, which conscious or unconscious, is adhesion to Christ himself. (v 29)

The human visibility of the director disappears in order to set the pace to faith, to Christ invisibly present (vv 30-31)

Enthusiastic conversion of the heart to the community, of those who were already leaving, a singular charismatic effect of inner fervor … and Christ had given no particular orders. He had simply wakened up, in the heart, the spontaneous desire of what He wanted to obtain. (vv 32-24)

48Direction must no be carried out in a negative sense, the director contenting himself with listening and correcting some defect, but, and above all, it must focused positively pointing to the acquisition of virtues, guiding, advising and encouraging great enterprises. The director has to, at the same time, remember that the directed person must live by himself, he must bear in mind that he fulfills the function of “crutches” not of “a wheel chair”.

49Directors should try to teach promptly to the souls that seek direction, to do it with the best order and possible fruitfulness, without losing time or without any useless digressions. For this, it is very helpful to bear in mind the aspects that should be dealt during the direction.

Spiritual life (particular examination, sacraments, prayers and penance, practice of the charity). In this area it is important to educate the directed person about how to confess: to distinguish imperfections and temptations. The director should also warn about the importance of not to confess “a list of venial sins” without any intention of emending them, he should recommend the usefulness of associating the confession with the particular exam.

The duties inherent to each state.

The doctrinal and spiritual formation (spiritual readings, studying of the Christian doctrine)

The apostolate (discernment to discover God’s will, rectitude of intention, selection and arrangement of activities according to its importance)

Chapter 2: In the internal life of the Institute.

Article 1: As regards the persons

50All member of the Institute, aware that the most difficult knowledge and which one avoids most, is the knowledge of oneself., should have a director28 and rely that, thanks to the spiritual direction he will be helped in the search of Christian perfection. God gives his grace to the person who uses the ordinary means for sanctity.

51It is vividly recommended to the members of the Institute the spiritual direction by priests of the same Institute, without detriment of the freedom that the Code of Canonical Law confers. The advantages that follow are many, among them: the specific help in the search of the perfection of the own state, according to the charisma and the aims of the Institute, the help in the conservation and the cultivation of the spirit of the founder, the possession of “a same thought and feeling"

52In conformity with the Code of Canonical Law29, those who are the very superiors of a house cannot assume the direction of the souls that are under his own responsibility. This gives them more freedom in their functions and in their duty of helping and correcting the religious in the disciplinary and external jurisdiction.

53All the priests of our Institute are qualified for the task of spiritual direction. That is why, they must never let themselves be intimidated by a false humility, scruples or shyness. Bearing this in mind, the older priest should encourage and drive the younger priests to the exercise of direction.

54A priest of our Institute must never think or feel himself the owner of the souls, not even give the impression that he has some power on the souls, or that he is zealous by the fact that others exercise direction. Furthermore, he must know how to lead the souls to other priests when necessary and be careful that the souls do not feel disorderly affection to his own person.

55Every priest that foresees being moved to other destination should, with enough time, advice the souls that are being directed by him, in the election of a new director. He should avoid, by reason of natural modesty or any other reason, any delay which would leave the souls without a director for some time.

56The members of the Institute should bear in mind that the direction and confession of the members among themselves is an excellent expression of delicate charity that must reign in the community.

57In the houses of formation there must be priests that have enough time and, if possible, be free of duties not pertaining to those houses, in order to attend the requirements of spiritual direction. Students should consider that they are strongly recommended to choose as their spiritual fathers, the spiritual directors assigned there. Nevertheless, the freedom that the Code of Canonic Law gives, to chose another priest, will always be present30

58Every priest of the Institute should have, as an absolute priority in his apostolate the attention and availability towards his brethren in his religious life. That is why, to encourage the visits, especially to those who are far away and isolated is one of the clearest expressions of exquisite charity.

Article 2: As regards the exercise.

59All the houses should have times and places for the practice of the direction and the confession, such as:

The diary time for the Adoration of the Blessed Sacrament.

The weekly penitential Liturgy

The monthly retires.

60The secret the subjects of the spiritual direction, must be observed strictly both by the director as well as by the directed person. The superiors or any other persons must keep even the appearance that they might wish to know any subjects of the spiritual direction31.

61The spiritual directors must be warned about some aberrations that may occur during the spiritual direction, such us

Their interference in the external jurisdiction of the government of the houses of the Institute

Their taking part of the play of those who want to use the direction for other purposes.

Their taking part of part of the play of those who change their directors easily, arguing false dialectical reasons. Therefore, directors should require from the directed person, enough reasons of spiritual benefit, in order to accept a change.

62In the houses of formation, the spiritual directors should procure to get, from the superiors, all information about the progress of their directed persons, having in mind a more efficacious direction. The superiors, should, at the same time, be informed about the frequent practice of the spiritual direction to the students. It is convenient that the superior of a house should know who the director of each person that is being formed is, and that he should inform the director about the news that has happened in the external jurisdiction which may help the director in his task.

63In other houses of the Institute, it seems convenient, when and if the Superior considers it opportune, if the Superior asks the director about it, that the director say to him, if the directed persons practice or not the direction. This may be useful specially to help to correct –paternally or fraternally, a certain member of the Institute.

Chapter 3: The external apostolate

64Obviously, many of the points considered above, are totally valid in the area of the apostolic activity, especially those referred to the spiritual direction.

65As regards the time, the places and the means for the exercise of spiritual direction, it is recommended:

The festive oratory for children and young people.

The Holy Hour established in the Parishes, Schools, Hospitals, etc.

The monthly retire of perseverance for laymen.

66It seems very convenient that the priests predicate about the marvelous benefits of the spiritual direction and of the frequent confession. They should insist, at the same time, to the persons that do spiritual exercises according to the method of Saint Ignatius, that they should incorporate the habitual spiritual direction in the reform of life.

67The priests must be convinced that it is in the personal dealing with the souls that takes place during the spiritual direction where the fruits of sanctity most pleasant to God are cultivated, and that it is there where the soul is helped to discern all types of motions or initiatives to discover God’s will on it.

68In the exercise of spiritual direction, the reasons and criteria to correct, discern, suggest or incite must always be supernatural. The director should be especially on guard against the prudence of the flesh.

69Finally, our priests and the whole Institute, should be known for the frequent pastoral practice of the confession and of the spiritual direction. People should know that everywhere they find a priest of our religious family, they will always find a spiritual father.

PARTE IV

OBJECT OF THE SPIRITUAL DIRECTION

Chapter 1: Education of the Christian attitudes.

70Spiritual direction aims to form Christian people that grow to the perfection of Jesus’ measure. There is one thing that is clear and cannot be replaced: it is the love to Christ what should be the principal thing for the directed person, a true falling in love with Christ. Beside Him, the Virgin and the Saints will occupy an important place. There should be flexibility in the rest. Thus, it should be procured that the director adapt himself to each directed person, according to the individual differences of each man, of one time and another, of the characters, and of the graces that God distributes.

71It is convenient to warn the directed about the temptation, especially in the beginning, of feeling an apparent hypocrisy in the practice of the direction, that he may have the impression of certain artificiality in his conduct. It must be taught that sincerity is not the adequacy between what is felt and what is expressed but between personal conviction and its expression. If any feelings that do not correspond to our personal conviction, should arise, they should be considered as "alien parasites"

72That is why, it must be sought that the activities of the directed persons should be, each time, further inmost. Spiritual activities have an efficacy of disposition, of physical not sacramental efficiency. They are instrumental, they are not principal they do not depend on the material execution of certain acts. Their doing must be

In spirit: they should not end in external action though they may use them as a means.

Cordial: the whole heart must take part of them.

Total: they should transform the whole man and all his manifestations.

73Spiritual direction must aim to form the person giving unity to the spiritual life. Sometimes one falls in the error of thinking that spiritual life occupies only a part of the life of man. On the contrary, the whole life must be spiritual and supernatural. Human being reaches this unification of his life by three fundamental attitudes: prayer (that gives him his vertical dimension and makes him “belong to God”), abnegation (that makes him, in a sense, not to belong to himself; it is the area of Christian abnegation, of external and inner renounce; it has its strong moment in God) and the active service to the brothers (that makes him belong to the others)32

74It must, at the same time seek to form a praying attitude. Spiritual direction must have as an objective to make the directed person reach a life of praying, that is, to make him live in the presence of God, and that his whole life be a living in a prayer of petition, in a state of immersion in God. The object of spiritual direction is not but to elevate the spiritual life, the life of union with God.

75It must seek, also, to form the person in the abnegation and mortification. The director must explain, for this reason, the evangelic concept of abnegation, and initiate the directed person into the meaning of the Cross, until the directed person reach “the wisdom of the Cross”, such as the great saints understood it, as Saint John of the Cross and Saint Louis Maria Grignion de Montfort.

76Finally, spiritual direction must have the goal of forming the directed person in the edification of the Church. The director must never lose sight of the fact that the sanctification always takes place in the Church and when the benefit of the Church is sought. The directed person is not an isolated soul but he belongs to a concrete ecclesial community, and is part of the mystic body of Christ. For that reason, direction will point to form in the directed person, the apostolic and missionary dimension, living up the illusions of taking the gospel to all the peoples, so that all the people believe in Christ.33

Chapter 2: The discernment of spirit as the objective of the spiritual direction.

77The progress in the spiritual life is manifested in a fidelity each time greater to God’s consent to man, not only in what refers to the election of the state of life once, but also in all particular cases, in such a way that the Christian faithful may understand God’s will in the different moments and may begin to set his hand to it with diligence. One of the aspects that spiritual direction must develop in the directed person is the exercise of distinguishing “God’s signs”, now objective (the signs of the times), then subjective (inner motions).

78Spiritual direction must initiate the directed person in the “discernment of spirits”, in other words, help the directed person to be conscious of how, during the development of the inner life, certain states of mind, inclinations, wishes, projects, temptations will arise. The director must orientate the directed person indicating the possible origin of these phenomena, giving concrete and precise norms which may help him to discern and act in each case.34

79At the same time, the director will help the directed person in the discernment in the moments of special difficulty in the spiritual life. He will have to attend and purify all that refers to the vocation and to the special charismas, detect possible spiritual illusions and help un the crisis proper to growth, now personal, then apostolic.

Chapter 3: Attention in cases of illnesses of the soul

80As a “doctor of souls”, the director must know how to distinguish certain illnesses of the soul:

Illnesses totally spiritual, such as spiritual mediocrity or coolness.

Illnesses with a physiological base, such as depressions, irascibility, spiritual apathy, etc.

Spiritual illnesses with psychological effects, especially perplexity of conscience in what refers to chastity and scruples.
